notes: Derived from this instance only: the grammar-construction subsystem of parsimonious at the injected revision, its five absorbed duty clusters, the four production modules touched, the callers re-threaded by the injection, and the failure modes a partial repair of this specific case would exhibit. Ownership words describe what must be true after a sound repair, not which class/helper names or file layout the repair must adopt: any equivalent re-homing that keeps each duty's observable contract satisfies a criterion.

rubrics.criterion: After the repair, no single class in the parsimonious production package owns three or more of the five formerly bundled responsibilities -- rule storage with default-rule dispatch, custom-callable classification and wrapping, string-literal evaluation with grammar-wide same-type enforcement, token-matcher construction with token-type bookkeeping, and rule-syntax registration with visitor-grammar assembly. The absorbed clusters were not transferred wholesale into one replacement owner; each cluster's state is reachable in the repaired tree from a home that does not also serve the other clusters.
rubrics.rationale: This is the central structural outcome of the case: the coordinator class dissolved, not relocated. It is answerable from the solver patch and repository alone by asking which methods share which instance or class state.

rubrics.criterion: Custom-callable rule handling -- classifying a callable as the 2-argument or 5-argument form, remembering that classification, and wrapping the callable into an expression node -- is implemented and holds its state outside the class that stores the rule map, while remaining reachable from grammar construction.
rubrics.rationale: This cluster arrived in the case with its own per-grammar cache and a deleted module-level factory; keeping it bundled with rule storage preserves exactly the cross-region coupling the task asks to remove.

rubrics.criterion: String-literal evaluation and the byte/str same-type record for a grammar are implemented and hold their state outside the rule-map class, and the record remains scoped to one whole grammar construction rather than to any single visitation pass.
rubrics.rationale: The literal record was absorbed from a visitor's instance state and a utilities helper; a sound repair gives the grammar-scoped question a grammar-reachable owner without returning it to the central class.

rubrics.criterion: Token-grammar construction duties -- deriving the token type from a literal spelling, constructing the token matcher, tracking the token types a grammar's rules mention, and refusing regexes in token grammars -- live outside the rule-map class and are reached from the token construction path through their new home.
rubrics.rationale: Token mode has its own ledger and its own policy in the injected tree; they travel together but do not belong with rule storage.

rubrics.criterion: The bookkeeping supporting rule-decorated visitor methods -- recording each decorated method's rule syntax so that metaclass-time assembly can find it -- is not implemented as class-level mutable state carried by the rule-map class, and the decorator and the metaclass reach their respective tagging and assembly services without routing through that class's instance-level registries.
rubrics.rationale: The registry was the last absorbed cluster and is the one whose home a repair can misjudge: assembly may legitimately remain a constructor concern, but the registry state itself must leave the central class.

rubrics.criterion: Every construction path is re-threaded end to end: building rules from text, building token rules, the import-time self-hosting bootstrap that defines the rule language, wrapping callable rules supplied at construction, and tagging/assembling rule-decorated visitor classes each obtain the services they need from the new owners, with no path left still calling a retired seam of the former coordinator.
rubrics.rationale: The injection touched each of these paths to route through the central class; leaving one path attached to the old seam is the most likely shape of an incomplete repair in this case.

rubrics.criterion: The rule-tree builder classes no longer hold a grammar back-reference whose only purpose is to let them call the absorbed registries on the central object, and the builders' literal and token hooks reach the owners of those duties directly or through whatever reference the repair's design supplies. A builder constructed with no arguments still acquires whatever it needs on demand.
rubrics.rationale: The back-reference threading is how the case couples otherwise-independent builders to the central class; a coherent repair rewires both ends of each of those references, not just the provider side.

rubrics.criterion: The wrapped expression produced for a custom callable still receives everything its calling forms need at match time: the 5-argument form still gets a working handle that reaches sibling rules, reports errors, and behaves like a grammar from the callable's point of view, and method-descriptor callables are resolved to their underlying functions before their form is classified.
rubrics.rationale: Moving the wrapping cluster without re-creating its closure over the owning grammar is the case's easiest silent break, so this associated change is graded as a fact about the repair, not a style point.

rubrics.criterion: Construction-time initialization was updated in step with the moves: whatever preparation each moved cluster needs now happens with its new owner, in an order that satisfies every consumer, and the rule-map class's constructor no longer performs preparation for state it no longer owns.
rubrics.rationale: The five regions were prepared by constructor-ordered hooks in the injected tree; a repair that moves code but leaves initialization split between old and new homes half-works.

rubrics.criterion: No vestige of the former arrangement is left live in the rule-map class: no unused initialization hooks or attributes whose state has moved away, no unused methods retained only to forward to a new owner when nothing needs the forwarding, and no state maintained simultaneously in both the old and new homes.
rubrics.rationale: Copied-rather-than-moved repairs leave orphaned hooks and duplicate records; this instance's injected seam (three constructor preparation hooks plus per-duty methods) makes such residue directly observable.

rubrics.criterion: No module-level machinery is left stranded by the moves: every import, helper, or class retained in a module after the repair is still used by live production code, including the AST/reflectivity machinery the grammar module gained when it absorbed literal evaluation and callable classification.
rubrics.rationale: The injection deliberately concentrated imports alongside the duties; a sound repair must trim both ends, so dead imports or dead helpers that only served the moved code are unrepaired residue specific to this case.

rubrics.criterion: Documentation traveled with the code or was corrected: no docstring or comment still claims that the grammar central class builds, classifies, records, or tracks any duty the repair moved elsewhere, and no owner's documentation describes duties it does not perform.
rubrics.rationale: The injected revision added a coordinator narrative to the central class and registry-ownership descriptions to the builders; leaving those claims in place after re-homing contradicts the repaired design, though it changes no behavior.

rubrics.criterion: Literal-type policing was not narrowed or scoped incorrectly: grammars that mix byte and str literals anywhere in their rules still fail construction with the message naming both literal spellings and their types, uniformly-typed grammars still construct, and no path (subgrammar copies, rebuilt grammars, the self-hosting meta-grammar, or a detached builder) produces literals that bypass the record.
rubrics.rationale: The enforcement is grammar-wide in the injected tree; splitting it per visitor pass or per sub-grammar is the plausible case-specific regression, since simple single-visitor grammars would still behave.

rubrics.criterion: Callable rules did not change form: the 2-argument and 5-argument conventions are still distinguished by signature at construction time, a wrong arity still raises the same construction-time error naming the offending argument count, and a callable reused by several rules is not newly classified or wrapped inconsistently between uses.
rubrics.rationale: Reclassification per use, late binding, or arity guessed at match time are exactly the mistakes the absorbed cache exists to prevent, so they are plausible failure modes of moving it.

rubrics.criterion: The self-hosting rule language still builds through the same facilities as user grammars: the meta-grammar that defines rule syntax is constructed by the repaired machinery with its literals subject to the same record and its rules to the same resolution, without a special-cased or duplicated path that lets bootstrap literals diverge from user-grammar literals.
rubrics.rationale: A repair can pass every user-facing path while quietly forking the bootstrap into an unpoliced copy; the import-time construction would still succeed, so the divergence is only visible by reading the repaired code.

rubrics.criterion: Decorated visitor classes did not lose registration semantics: first-decorated-by-source-line still picks the default rule, an overridden decorated method on a subclass does not strand or duplicate its syntax, metaclass selection still observes decorated methods, and visitor classes with no decorated methods remain unchanged.
rubrics.rationale: Registry-keying and override interplay are the subtlest behavior in the absorbed registration cluster and the least covered by ordinary construction tests.

rubrics.criterion: Token grammars did not lose their mode-specific behavior: token matchers still match by token type, and using a regex in a token grammar still fails during construction with the message about regexes not making sense for pre-lexed tokens -- not with a different error type raised from a different place.
rubrics.rationale: Moving the ledger and the refusal may preserve parsing while quietly changing when, how, or from where the refusal surfaces, which is the case-specific regression mode for the token cluster.

rubrics.criterion: Every per-grammar record introduced or retained by the repair stays scoped to a single grammar instance: records are not shared across grammars (class-level leakage would let one grammar's literals or token types contaminate another's construction answers) and are not recreated per literal or per visit where the record's purpose is one answer per grammar.
rubrics.rationale: Thinking a per-grammar registry is per-construction and hanging it on the new owner at the wrong level is an easy mistake once the state moves; two grammars built back to back expose it.
